$comment: The authoritative dependency graph of the Core Course. Validated by scripts/check-course-graph.py; proved acyclic in lean/CourseGraph. Chapters are listed in dependency order: every dependency must reference a chapter earlier in this file.

stages.title: Reasoning
stages.blurb: Logic, sets, relations, functions. No numbers.

stages.title: Expanding the line
stages.blurb: Z, Q, primes, congruences, and the first crisis.

stages.title: The continuum
stages.blurb: R constructed; completeness; cardinality; ordinals; choice.

stages.title: Completing algebra
stages.blurb: Polynomials, C, and the FTA debt.

stages.title: Structure and linear algebra
stages.blurb: Categories and linear algebra over R and C.

stages.title: Euclidean analysis
stages.blurb: Convergence, series, continuity, derivatives, integration, the elementary functions, ODEs. Discharges the multivariable debts.

stages.title: The canvas
stages.blurb: The canvas: spaces, compactness, quotients, approximation.

stages.title: Measure
stages.blurb: Sigma-algebras to Fourier, ending at the probability laws.

stages.title: Calculus as linearisation
stages.blurb: Manifolds, tangent spaces, forms, Stokes, curvature.

stages.title: Complex analysis
stages.blurb: Holomorphy, Cauchy, residues, and the FTA proved: the ledger closes.

stages.title: Algebra and symmetry
stages.blurb: Groups, rings, Galois, Lie groups, and the geometry synthesis.

stages.title: The functional summit
stages.blurb: Functional analysis to elliptic PDE: Banach and Hilbert spaces, distributions, Sobolev, the Laplacian's spectrum.

stages.title: Topology and geometry at research level
stages.blurb: Homotopy, homological algebra, homology, de Rham cohomology, characteristic classes, Riemannian geometry, representations.

stages.title: Probability at research level
stages.blurb: Martingales, Brownian motion, the Ito calculus, and the diffusion bridge to PDE.

chapters.title: Propositions, quantifiers, and what a proof is
Sets: membership, products, power sets
Relations: order, equivalence
Functions: injections, surjections, bijections, composition
Proof strategies in action: the false proof, dissected
chapters.note: The dissected false proof is the quantifier swap (forall-exists implies exists-forall). H2 calls back: uniform continuity is the swapped form of continuity, and compactness is what makes the swap legal.

chapters.title: The Peano axioms: what counting is
chapters.note: The Peano declarations define the counting numbers (any two systems satisfying them are interchangeable); they are content, not course axioms. The adopted axioms remain classical logic and choice.

chapters.title: Addition defined recursively; its laws proved

declaredInputs.note: That the two defining lines yield exactly one function; the general primitive-recursion theorem is Stage D's transfinite recursion.

chapters.title: Multiplication, order, exponentiation: all theorems
Division with remainder; the Archimedean property
Counting arguments: bijections, permutations, and the binomial theorem
chapters.note: Counting as bijections; factorials, permutations and combinations; the binomial theorem and Pascal's triangle; the pigeonhole principle. The finite ancestor of the series chapter's binomial series.

chapters.title: The failure of subtraction; Z as difference classes
chapters.note: The integers as difference classes: pairs of counting numbers modulo A3's equivalence relation, with well-defined arithmetic (the add_wd formal witness compiles in CI).

chapters.title: The failure of division; Q as fraction classes; density
The first crisis: x^2 = 2 has no rational solution
Primes and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic
chapters.note: The Euclidean algorithm and Bezout's identity come first; linear Diophantine equations are the exercises. Unique factorisation is proved on Bezout's shoulders.

chapters.title: Congruence classes and the rings Z/nZ
chapters.note: Congruence as an equivalence relation; the ring Z/nZ; units mod p; Fermat's little theorem. Feeds the examples of the algebra stage.

chapters.title: Dedekind cuts: R constructed from order alone
Arithmetic and completeness of R, proved
chapters.note: Completeness is stated as the supremum property and proved for the cuts. The Cauchy-sequence construction is rebuilt and proved equivalent to D1's cuts once convergence exists (Stage G).

chapters.title: Decimals, roots, the place of Q inside R
Cardinality: countable Q, uncountable R
Ordinals and transfinite induction
chapters.note: Well-ordered sets and their classification; ordinals as the sizes of well-orderings; transfinite recursion and induction: the instruments the choice chapter uses.

chapters.title: Choice, Zorn's lemma, and well-ordering
chapters.note: The axiom of choice is adopted here (course map axiom table), and Zorn's lemma and well-ordering are proved equivalent to it. Spent by Stage F's basis theorem, Stage L's maximal ideals, and Stage H's Tychonoff.

chapters.title: Polynomials as formal objects
chapters.note: Polynomials as coefficient sequences: identity is syntactic (refuted over Z/2), Horner evaluation is the formal witness (evalPoly, compiling in CI).

chapters.title: C built as pairs with a multiplication rule
The fundamental theorem of algebra: statement, consequences, and the debt

declaredInputs.note: Declared here as a working axiom; discharged by the winding-number proof in K3.

chapters.title: Categories: objects, morphisms, universal properties, adjunctions
Vector spaces, linear maps, dimension

declaredInputs.note: Basis existence for spaces that are not finitely generated.

chapters.title: Duality and the double dual
Quotient spaces and their universal property
Determinants as alternating forms
Exterior algebra
Eigenstructure, triangularisation, Cayley-Hamilton

declaredInputs.note: Used via E3's declaration; the root guarantee for complex triangularisation.

chapters.title: Inner products, orthogonality, the spectral theorem
Canonical forms: what remains when diagonalisation fails
chapters.note: The Jordan and rational canonical forms; the singular value decomposition from F8's spectral theorem; Sylvester's law of inertia. Every way a linear map refuses to diagonalise, named and normalised.

chapters.title: Convergence of sequences in R and R^n
chapters.note: limsup and liminf; subsequence principles; the Cauchy construction of R rebuilt and proved equivalent to the cuts of D1.

chapters.title: Series and the exchange of limits
chapters.note: Numeric series (comparison, ratio, root, alternating), then sequences of functions: pointwise versus uniform, the Weierstrass M-test, and what uniformity licenses (limits, sums, derivatives term by term). Closes by rereading decimals as series.

chapters.title: Continuity in several variables
The derivative in several variables
chapters.note: The one-variable slice carries Rolle, the mean value theorem, monotonicity, and L'Hopital: EVT and IVT cashed in.

chapters.title: The chain rule, partials, and Clairaut
The inverse function theorem
chapters.note: The inverse and implicit function theorems, proved together; graphs versus level sets.

chapters.title: The exponential and trigonometric functions via power series
chapters.note: Power series, the general binomial series, and the classical functions re-derived; e and pi meet their series.

chapters.title: Integration on the real line and the fundamental theorem of calculus
chapters.note: Darboux's theory, the fundamental theorem of calculus, and Taylor's theorem with integral remainder.

chapters.title: The contraction mapping principle and existence for ODEs
Metric and topological spaces, continuity, homeomorphism

declaredInputs.note: Debt paid: D2 constructs R and proves completeness, so this is no longer a declaration.
Continuity of sin, cos, exp used in examples and exercises.

chapters.title: Connectedness and compactness; the IVT and EVT
chapters.note: Compactness is presented as the theorem that legalises the A5 quantifier swap: continuity under an existential quantifier becomes uniformity under a universal one.

chapters.title: Completeness, the Baire category theorem, and metrisation
chapters.note: Complete metric spaces and Cantor's nested theorem; Baire category; separation axioms; Urysohn metrisation; compactness equivalences.

chapters.title: Approximation and compactness in function spaces
chapters.note: Bernstein polynomials and the Weierstrass approximation theorem; Stone-Weierstrass (the density engine of the Fourier chapter); Arzela-Ascoli: compactness for families of functions.

chapters.title: The quotient topology: gluing and its price
chapters.note: The universal property of the quotient; the circle as an interval with its ends glued; projective spaces; why quotients can fail to be Hausdorff, and what that costs.

chapters.title: Sigma-algebras and measures
The Lebesgue integral: Caratheodory
chapters.note: The comparison theorem: Riemann integrable on a bounded interval means Lebesgue integrable with the same value, and equals a.e. continuity. G8's integral is the special case, not a rival.

chapters.title: Modes of convergence
L^p spaces and duality
Product measures and Fubini-Tonelli; the change-of-variables formula
Radon-Nikodym, conditional expectation, and the birth of probability
chapters.note: The Lebesgue differentiation theorem; functions of bounded variation; absolutely continuous functions and the fundamental theorem of calculus in its correct generality.

chapters.title: Fourier series and the Fourier transform
The laws of large numbers and the central limit theorem
chapters.note: The Borel-Cantelli lemmas: the measure-theoretic grammar of 'almost always' and 'infinitely often'.

chapters.title: Smooth manifolds: charts, atlases, smooth maps
Tangent spaces, the differential, the IFT on manifolds

declaredInputs.note: One-variable FTC, proved in the integration chapter of Stage G.
Hadamard's smoothness argument; discharged by the product-measure machinery.

chapters.title: Differential forms and the exterior derivative
Partitions of unity
chapters.note: Covered inside the Stokes page: the gluing construction and its covering-of-a-manifold applications.

chapters.title: Integration, orientation, and Stokes

declaredInputs.note: J4 builds the partition machinery this chapter's proof consumes.

chapters.title: Submanifolds, immersions, regular level sets
Connections, curvature, and geodesics
Holomorphy: complex differentiability and its rigidity
chapters.note: Conformal maps, Mobius transformations, the Riemann sphere; harmonic functions as the real and imaginary parts of holomorphy.

chapters.title: Complex integration, Cauchy's theorem, residues
chapters.note: Taylor and Laurent series; the argument principle and Rouche's theorem; residue calculus.

chapters.title: The fundamental theorem of algebra, proved - the ledger closes
Groups through the categorical lens
chapters.note: Subgroups, quotients, Lagrange; group actions, orbits and the class equation; the Sylow theorems.

chapters.title: Rings and modules

declaredInputs.note: Existence of maximal ideals and of maximal ideals in a quotient.

chapters.note: Tensor products of modules with their universal property; multilinear maps rehabilitated from F6 in the generality algebra needs.

chapters.title: Galois theory: symmetry of equations
chapters.note: Field extensions, automorphism groups, the fundamental theorem; constructibility, solvable groups, Abel-Ruffini, and the cubic and quartic resolved.

chapters.title: Lie groups and group actions
chapters.note: Topological groups and orbit spaces: H5's quotient topology earns its keep here first.

chapters.title: Geometry: the fifth postulate, its collapse, and symmetry as geometry
chapters.note: Synthesis, not reintroduction: Hilbert's axioms re-seen, the equivalent postulate forms proved equivalent, the Poincaré and hyperboloid models built analytically, curvature explaining the failure, Erlangen closing the arc. The closing chord of the core spine; the research stages M, N and O continue past it.

chapters.title: Banach spaces and the four pillars
chapters.note: The Riesz representation theorem for C([a,b])* as the bridge back to Stage I's measure.

chapters.title: Hilbert spaces and the spectral theorem for compact operators
chapters.note: The infinite-dimensional completion of F8: compact operators, the Fredholm alternative, eigenfunction expansions. Sturm-Liouville as the first instance.

chapters.title: Weak topologies, locally convex spaces, and distributions
chapters.note: Banach-Alaoglu; weak and weak-* convergence; the Schwartz space with the Fourier transform as an automorphism of it; distributions as its dual, and the derivative extended to all of them.

chapters.title: Banach algebras, the Gelfand spectrum, and C*-algebras
chapters.note: The spectral radius via Liouville (K2 pays again); characters and the Gelfand transform; commutative C*-algebras are algebras of continuous functions: Gelfand-Naimark.

chapters.title: Sobolev spaces and weak derivatives
chapters.note: The regularity ladder: weak derivatives, Sobolev embedding, traces; why elliptic equations are solved in these spaces.

chapters.title: Elliptic theory: the Laplacian, Fredholm, and regularity
chapters.note: Weak solutions become smooth; the Laplacian's spectrum as the infinite spectral theorem in action; Hodge theory on the horizon.

chapters.title: Unbounded operators, the spectral theorem, and Stone's theorem
chapters.note: Self-adjointness beyond boundedness; the spectral theorem in its general form via projection-valued measures; Stone's theorem: one-parameter unitary groups and their generators. The mathematical frame of quantum mechanics.

chapters.title: The fundamental group, covering spaces, and Van Kampen
chapters.note: Loops modulo homotopy as a group; the circle's group computed; Van Kampen's theorem.

chapters.title: Homological algebra: chain complexes, derived functors, Ext and Tor
chapters.note: Abelian categories as the abstract habitat of exact sequences, stated as a remark; the concrete categories of modules carry the chapter.

chapters.title: Homology: simplicial and singular
chapters.note: Higher homotopy groups are defined and their computability gap stated honestly: computations beyond this course are research.

chapters.title: de Rham cohomology: Stokes as an isomorphism
chapters.note: The Poincare lemma; the degree of a map; Poincare duality on oriented manifolds; the de Rham theorem stated.

chapters.title: Fibre bundles, connections, and characteristic classes
chapters.note: Chern-Weil theory: curvature integrates into cohomology classes that see the topology of the bundle.

chapters.title: Riemannian geometry: Hopf-Rinow, Gauss-Bonnet, comparison
chapters.note: Geodesic completeness equals topological completeness; Gauss-Bonnet as the marriage of curvature and topology; comparison geometry's triangle intuitions made theorems.

chapters.title: Representation theory: characters and Peter-Weyl
chapters.note: Fourier generalised: irreducible representations as the modes of a group. Finite groups by characters; compact groups by Peter-Weyl.

chapters.title: Martingales and optional stopping
chapters.note: Conditional expectation as the engine; filtrations; the optional sampling theorem; upcrossing inequalities.

chapters.title: Brownian motion: construction, invariance, pathologies
chapters.note: Kolmogorov's extension theorem; Donsker's invariance principle as a statement; continuous paths that are nowhere differentiable.

chapters.title: The Ito calculus
chapters.note: Quadratic variation as the obstruction to the ordinary chain rule; the Ito integral; Ito's formula.

chapters.title: Stochastic differential equations and Feynman-Kac
chapters.note: Existence and uniqueness by Picard iteration - G9 returns; the diffusion semigroup solves the PDE, and Feynman-Kac fuses the course's two halves: analysis and probability are one subject.

chapters.title: Martingale representation, Girsanov, and the risk-neutral measure
chapters.note: Every martingale is an Ito integral (representation); changing the measure via the Radon-Nikodym derivative (Girsanov); the risk-neutral calculus that pricing theory is built on.

axioms.statement: Every proposition is either true or false, and a proof may use the law of the excluded middle.
axioms.note: Adopted at A1. Constructive alternatives are not developed; a proof by contradiction is therefore always available.

axioms.statement: For every family of nonempty sets there is a function choosing one element from each set.
axioms.note: Adopted at D6, where it is shown equivalent to Zorn's lemma and to the well-ordering principle.
